title: What debug commands do you use?
author: Binary-Trees
selftext:
Do you make a debug console and commands to do things such as give money and spawn mobs for testing?

What are your most clever debug tools/tricks you use for the human part of your playtesting?

comments.author: NebulaRisingGame
comments.body: Build test automation, auditing tools, and an observability dashboard.  The dashboard is super useful if your game tracks and logs it's data so you can analyze the player experience and balancing.

replies.author: Binary-Trees
replies.body: Nice! Im interested in the dashboard. What is that? Is it a easy-to-view display of all the variables in use?

replies.author: NebulaRisingGame
replies.body: Depending on your game and what data you want to track.  I build timeline data charts and widgets to alert on degradation and any other thresholds you want to monitor, leveling rate, gold generation, etc.  At the player level, guild level and game levels

comments.author: Stinky_You
comments.body:
My debug menu (f1) got cluttered really fast (it's on the list to fix soon) because it has sliders for almost every value for everything, most of which I don't use because balancing will have to wait until more gameplay elements are implemented (equipment, equipment upgrades, passives (from different sources)). 

Started with f1 (values) and f2 (misc. Spawn enemy, invincible, location/scene switch) debug menus, now f3 will take and put a screenshot + my note in a folder for Claude to address and delete so screenshots don't clutter chat sessions.

I'm also looking for debug menu advice

replies.author: Binary-Trees
replies.body: Wow that's genius. Thanks for sharing. I wonder if it might be worth a similar screenshot and note workflow that creates a github issue for tracking.

replies.author: Stinky_You
replies.body: NP, seems like not very many people are into sharing? I also check other subs for tips and am slowly clawing my way past Claude academy, but most of that is stuff I won't use
